title: apply_dao_ack can reinstall an older Success ACK after a newer one
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness / robustness

ShortAddressAssignmentClient::apply_dao_ack() ignores an ACK when dao_sequence != expected_sequence, and only fingerprints last_ack when last_sequence == dao_sequence. It never requires dao_sequence to be newer than last_sequence (RFC 6550 Section 7.2).

If a node has two outstanding DAOs (ALLOCATE seq=5 then RELEASE seq=6 before the first ACK), ACKs can arrive out of order:
1. Success RELEASE seq=6 with expected_sequence=6 installs assigned_short=None and last_sequence=6
2. Delayed Success ALLOCATE seq=5 with expected_sequence=5 (still outstanding) skips the fingerprint check because last_sequence is 6, then overwrites assigned_short with the old address

Non-success ACKs (Exhausted/Invalid) return Ok(false) without storing last_ack/last_sequence, so a later Success for that same sequence also installs.

This is not a refile of project-LICHEN-worker6-k1da (ACK operation not bound to the outstanding request at one sequence) or project-LICHEN-worker6-frdf (raw-wire fingerprint and 40-byte cap). Fix: reject Success ACKs that are not newer than last_sequence (equal sequence stays the identical-retransmit path), and bind a sequence to the first accepted status/operation so Exhausted then Success cannot upgrade.
